_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4314 — `FrontmatterService.parseObject` list continuation plus the paired write-side span. Each mutant is type-preserving (an impossible-but-valid regex / an alternative return), never `if (false)`, so a red is a behaviour difference and not a compile failure (integration-test-revert-verify §A36). `red_re` anchors on the `● <suite> › [Xn]` failure header rather than a bare key, because jest echoes neighbouring `it(...)` source lines in its diff context (§A44/§A104).
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/core/src/utilities/FrontmatterService.ts

M1_continuation_line_ends_the_array._note: The pre-#4314 behaviour for a CONTINUATION line: a block-scalar body / nested-map sub-key falls through to flushArray(), so the array ends there and every item after it is lost from the read — and both primitives then write the truncated list back. Comment shapes are NOT here: their carve-out sits in its own branch above (M5/M9).

M2_blank_line_ends_the_array._note: Blanks are no longer held back, so a blank line INSIDE a block-scalar body ends the array — the write side (findPropertyLineSpan) absorbs exactly such a blank, so this is the half that would put the two out of step again.

M3_two_space_items_only._note: Item regex back to two-space-only: a column-0 list reads as an empty array again, and property_append then writes its single new item above the orphaned originals.

M4_flow_sequence_read_as_scalar._note: Flow-style arrays fall through to the scalar branch (pre-#4314): property_append nests the whole flow text inside one item and property_replace refuses the property as 'not a list'.

M5_comment_absorbed_into_the_item._note: Without the carve-out an interleaved `#` comment is treated as a value line: BETWEEN items it is absorbed into the item above (corrupting that item's value, which breaks the Set-based dedup and writes a duplicate alias) and BEFORE the first item it ends the array, so the property reads as empty and the rewrite erases every alias.

M6_span_does_not_own_column0_items._note: The paired WRITE-side half: the key's span stops at its own line, so the rewritten list is spliced above the original column-0 items and they are left dangling — js-yaml then refuses the whole document. Reddens the disk axis only; the read axis (P3) is unaffected, which is exactly why the read fix alone would have been a half-fix.

M7_malformed_flow_accepted._note: The splitter's fail-safe: an unterminated quote would yield invented items instead of leaving the value as the opaque scalar it was before #4314.

M8_closing_before_opening_accepted._note: The depth<0 guard is NOT redundant with the final depth check: `]] [[` closes before it opens and ends at depth 0, so only this guard rejects it.

M9_comment_before_first_item_still_termi._note: The carve-out narrowed back to a NON-EMPTY array (`openItems`), i.e. what my first cut of this fix did: a comment BETWEEN items is handled, one BEFORE the first item still ends the array. That is the shape all 33 live carriers have, and a corpus-wide old-vs-new diff of parseObject over 53 591 assets is what caught it — the between-items fixture alone could not.

M10_unquoted_wikilink_split_as_flow._note: The regression this PR introduced and then closed (review of #4381): without the `[[` exclusion an unquoted `exo__Instance_class: [[ems__Task]]` satisfies the bracket test, splits to the item `[ems__Task]` — one bracket pair short — and the rewrite puts that on disk, where it is unrecoverable and a second cycle is a stable fixed point. Reddens the round-trip axis only; the quoted flow axes stay green because `["..."]` does not start with `[[`.
